root_cause: The LinkedIn revenue cockpit generated and prioritized evidence-backed actions, but the canonical social delivery path did not consume eligible cockpit actions. This left supported LinkedIn post-reply actions dependent on manual cockpit operation.
prevention_rules: The cockpit is an observability and exception surface, not the primary execution surface.
Eligible LinkedIn post-reply actions must be atomically claimed before any provider call.
Only provider capabilities actually available through the connected LinkedIn transport may execute automatically.
Unsupported DM and connection activation actions must remain explicit capability exceptions; never fabricate or bypass transport capabilities.
Provider acknowledgement and canonical outcome writeback are required before an action is marked executed.
Every new RPC used by material runtime code must be registered in the quality-surface contract.
A provider comment id is an irreversible side-effect boundary: outcome/writeback failure must set reconciliation_required and republish_forbidden, never return the action to suggested.

replay_scenarios: evidence-backed LinkedIn post reply is claimed once, executed through Composio, and written back with provider/outcome evidence
unsupported LinkedIn DM or connection activation stays an explicit capability exception
concurrent publisher runs cannot execute the same suggested action twice

queue_canary.reason: Current top suggested queue contained only unsupported LinkedIn DM/news actions, so the live canary correctly produced no external comment side effect.

production_readback.note: Runtime integration is live and proven. A real LinkedIn comment side effect has not yet been observed because no eligible reply_post action was present during verification; unsupported DM/connection actions remain fail-closed.
